guarantees.claim: On active-low asynchronous reset (rst_ni = 0), msg_allowed is cleared to 0 immediately, regardless of clock.
When hash_start_or_continue is high at a rising clock edge, msg_allowed is set to 1, even if packer_flush_done is simultaneously high (priority of first if branch).
When hash_start_or_continue is low and packer_flush_done is high at a rising clock edge, msg_allowed is set to 0.
guarantees.cond: posedge clk_i, rst_ni high, hash_start_or_continue == 0, packer_flush_done == 1

guarantees.claim: When no control condition is active (hash_start_or_continue and packer_flush_done both low) and reset is deasserted, msg_allowed retains its previous value.
guarantees.cond: posedge clk_i, rst_ni high, hash_start_or_continue == 0, packer_flush_done == 0

assumptions.claim: To ensure msg_allowed is cleared between messages, the source of hash_start_or_continue and packer_flush_done must avoid asserting packer_flush_done while hash_start_or_continue is asserted; otherwise msg_allowed will not drop to 0 before the new message.
assumptions.cond: When the protocol requires msg_allowed == 0 between message operations
assumptions.risk: Simultaneous assertion keeps msg_allowed high through the start of a new message, potentially allowing data injection before the hash engine is properly configured for the new message.

uncertain_points.claim: When hash_start_or_continue and packer_flush_done are both true at a clock edge, the RTL gives priority to hash_start_or_continue, leaving msg_allowed high. It is unclear if this prioritised handling is intentional and safe for all message sequences.
uncertain_points.cond: both signals active on same posedge clk_i
uncertain_points.risk: If msg_allowed must be low between messages to reset internal state or handshake, the lack of a clear could cause state corruption or mis-framing.
